answer: Each identity must solve a fresh per-epoch puzzle whose kernel is a seed unique to its address; grading is no velvet glove, since answers are machine-checked for the required tokens and human-judged for coherence. Minting a thousand jade-polished sybils buys nothing, because each one still owes the same irreducible compute-and-judgment cost. The economy prices identity by work actually done, not by raw head count.
